tutorial.title: Interacting with Webpages
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to make JavaScript and HTML work together.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Behind every fun browser game, there's some JavaScript code.

In this mini game screen, JavaScript changes the score when you click the gain points button.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
To add JavaScript code to a game webpage, we start with the <script> and </script> tags.

Make sure to pick <script>, followed by </script>.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
The script element is the last element before the closing </body> tag in the HTML structure.

Make sure to pick <h3>Dungeon Runner, followed by </h3>, and finally <script>.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Similar to CSS, we use a separate file to write JavaScript. To do this, we include a src attribute that links to the file we want to use.

Make sure to pick src, followed by =, and finally "script.js".

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
In the JS file, we can write JavaScript like const playerName = "Lee";.

Make sure to pick const, followed by playerName, and finally "Lee".

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
The JavaScript runs automatically when the webpage displays. Find the output of console.log(playerName) in the Output tab.

Make sure to pick playerName, followed by playerName.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which tags do we use to add JavaScript code to HTML?

<script> and </script><style> and <style>

<script> and </script>.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
Where in the HTML structure do we add the script element?

In the last position in the body elementAnywhere in the body element

In the last position in the body element.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
Where does the JavaScript code go?

Inside the JavaScript fileAnywhere inside the body element

Inside the JavaScript file.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we run the code in the JavaScript file linked via the script element?

It runs automatically when the webpage displaysWe have to add a special instruction

It runs automatically when the webpage displays.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the opening script tag.

Make sure to pick < followed by script and then src="script.js", >, </script>.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
Insert the elements in their correct positions.

Make sure to pick <script src="script.js"></script>, followed by </body>.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Link to script.js using the src attribute.

Make sure to type src="script.js".

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the sum of the gems and coins variables.

Make sure to pick console, followed by log, and finally +.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent: We've seen how we can add JavaScript to our HTML files. Now let's use the script tags to interact with game UI elements.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
To tell the elements how to respond to, say, an attack button click, we need to identify them.

To identify the elements we want to interact with, we can give each of them a unique id. Let's add an ID to the p element.

Make sure to pick id, followed by =, and finally "health".

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can access the HTML elements of our game screen using the document keyword. document represents our webpage.

Now, to interact with an HTML element, we need the document.getElementById() instruction.

Make sure to pick document, followed by getElementById.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Inside document.getElementById() we place the ID of the element we want to interact with, like health here.

Make sure to pick document followed by getElementById and then (, "health", ).

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Interactive game screens often use buttons to react to clicks from players.

However, without more information, a button tag is useless. To react to clicks from players, a button tag needs the onclick attribute.

Make sure to pick onclick.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
The onclick attribute can call functions when a player clicks on the button. Set onclick to "attack()".

In this function, we can add the code to trigger the behavior we want. Check script.js to see the function the button will call.

Make sure to pick =, followed by "attack()".

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use the attack function to change the content of an element, like its text, when we click a button.

First, access the text of the p with the innerHTML instruction.

Make sure to pick ., followed by innerHTML.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
Now that we have accessed the text of the p element, we can change it.

Set the text of the p element to "HP: 90".

Make sure to pick =, followed by "HP: 90".

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which instruction do we use to access an element?

document.getElementById()getElementById()

Make sure to pick document.getElementById().

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
What can we use IDs for?

To identify HTML elements and interact with them using JavaScriptTo display similar elements

To identify HTML elements and interact with them using JavaScript.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which instruction accesses the paragraph?

document.getElementById("score")document.getElementById("scoreTitle")

Make sure to pick document.getElementById("score").

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which attribute retrieves the text of an HTML element?

.innerHTML.text

Make sure to pick .innerHTML.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the text of the paragraph after the button is clicked?

Potion added to inventoryPick up the potion

Potion added to inventory.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with this code?

None of the HTML elements has an id called bossHealthinnerHTMLshould be INNERhtml

None of the HTML elements has an id called bossHealth.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the onclick attribute do?

It defines what happens when players click a buttonIt takes players to another website

It defines what happens when players click a button.

lessons.title: Lesson #16
lessons.interactiveContent:
Upon clicking on the Magic button, change the game level name by updating the heading's text.

Make sure to pick document.getElementById("levelName") followed by .innerHTML and then =, "Level 2: The Cave".

lessons.title: Lesson #17
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the attribute to react to clicks from players.

Make sure to pick onclick.

lessons.title: Lesson #18
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set the value of the onclick attribute to call the respawn function when a player clicks on the button.

Make sure to pick "respawn()".
